newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan cements up on President Lee promise.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan cements up on President Lee promise.

text.p: Taiwan's cement shares rose at mid-morning on Monday after President Lee Teng-hui promised at the weekend the government would solve businesses' problems with obtaining land within six months, brokers said.
After 90 minutes, cements rose 1.24 percent while the overall index was up 0.86 percent.
Lucky Cement rose 90 cents, or 3.26 percent, to T$28.5 and Taiwan Cement gained T$1, or 1.77 percent, to T$57.5.
"President Lee's promise gives hope that domestic demand-oriented industries, especially cement, will have no problem in obtaining land needed for expansion," said Eric Liu of National Securities.
Taiwan Cement alone has said it plans to invest T$80 billion to build a cement zone in the northeastern county of Hualien if it can obtain necessary land and pass environmental examination.
